Kudos and thanks for that. However, another element exists that can be greatly improved and probably just got missed; and hopefully can be added. It would't be too difficult to do a simple if/exists > show view/share icon else/doesn't > show save icon (as it is now). This will spare the need to save multiple duplicates and incrementing it when you can simply provide a visual check that it has already been saved. It is simply better UX and cleaner that way. Steps to reproduce.  save an item save it again you have a duplicate with a -1 at the end save it again you now have 3 with a -1 and -2 of the same item repeat and goes on as long as you keep saving Expected result: Detect that the item has already been saved and either provide a view icon or share icon to visually indicate it has been saved already, otherwise show the save button. A simple file system check for the item will facilitate this. Thanks in advance.

verdict.text:
## Summary
The model catches all 4 gold-incomplete requirements (83, 496, 592, 1504), but it also marks 17 complete requirements as incomplete, so verdict precision is only 0.19. The main weakness runs opposite to the risk the experiment targets: the model writes `<MISSING_ACTOR> <MISSING_MODAL_VERB>` where all three annotators wrote "the App must". The scope and condition results are also unreliable, because the scorer appears to misread them.

## Missing-slot detection
The scope and condition numbers look like a scorer artifact rather than invented content. The LLM outputs for 496, 592, 2943 and 937 contain no scope or condition text and no placeholder either. The scorer still records both slots as "filled", which would explain scope flagged 0 of 34 and condition 1 of 21. One condition is a real fill: 245 adds "While the mobile device is a dual SIM device". One human annotator wrote the same thing, so it is defensible. The true condition flag rate cannot be known until absent slots are scored as missing.

Actor and modalVerb are over-flagged, not filled. The single gold-missing case of each is caught, but there are 20 and 17 false flags on slots the gold marks implied. The model is skipping the Rimay convention of a default actor and "must".

Action shows the real fabrication. For 496, 592 and 83, the gold (2 of 3 annotators) says the action is missing, yet the model wrote one from the title, e.g. "support emoji". 1504 was flagged correctly. With 4 cases, a 0.25 recall is one requirement's worth of signal.

## Conversion quality
The model reaches about 85% of the human-human ceiling on sequence ratio and about 92% on cosine. Part of the gap is structural: the humans always start with `<MISSING_SCOPE>, <MISSING_CONDITION>,` and the model leaves this out, which lowers the character-level scores in particular.

Most Paska failures come from the placeholder habit, not from bad requirements. Pass rate is 0.71 when the model kept an actor and modal verb, and 0.19 when it emitted placeholders. Of the 21 failures, 15 are "Not requirement", the smell Paska raises when a sentence has no actor or modal verb. Only "Not precise verb" (1283, 7310) and "Non-atomic requirement" (6457) point to problems in the content itself.

## Anomalies
- **Text outside the answer block:** 828-Signal (61 characters). It is cosmetic and its scores look normal.
- **Atomic requirement flagged `<NON_ATOMIC>`:** 2055-Signal and 7345-Signal. Both have a present condition, which suggests the model reads "condition + response" as two units. 7345 has the lowest similarity among Paska-passing items (0.30). With only 2 of 35 affected, the headline numbers barely move.
- **Not in the anomaly list:** 6457-Signal packed two actions into one sentence, which is the reverse error.

## Next step
- Fix the parser so that a slot absent from the output counts as `missing` rather than `filled`, or require all five slots explicitly in the prompt. Then rerun Track 1 before comparing strategies.
- Add one line to the prompt: an implied actor is "the App" and an implied modal verb is "must". Then check whether the false flags and the "Not requirement" smells drop together.
- Spot-check whether filling the action from the title (496, 592, 83) should count as fabrication; it is a judgement call where the annotators split 2 to 1.
